content.value_statement: Paid campaigns can waste budget when conversions, UTMs, and attribution rules are inconsistent. This skill creates a practical pre-flight review and a reusable event specification from your exports and test conversion.
actual_capabilities: Creates a pass, fail, or needs-input pre-flight checklist for conversion tracking.
Reviews GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports supplied by the user.
Builds a consistent UTM naming convention without personal data in parameters.
Defines conversion events, values, currencies, and stable deduplication identifiers.
Flags attribution-window mismatches, offline import gaps, and iOS-ATT modeled gaps.
States launch readiness and routes scoring work to the related account-audit skill.
limitations: It relies on exports and test results that the user provides.
It does not access Google Ads, Meta, GTM, or pixel APIs by default.
It does not quantify double counting or perform incrementality analysis.
It does not score ROAS readiness or make budget decisions.

use_cases.title: Check a campaign before launch
use_cases.description: Review a planned Google and Meta campaign for event firing, UTM coverage, and launch blockers.

use_cases.title: Standardize account measurement
use_cases.description: Create a shared UTM and conversion-event specification for a multi-channel advertising account.

use_cases.title: Investigate reporting differences
use_cases.description: Identify likely UTM, attribution-window, and deduplication gaps behind differences between platform and GA4 reports.

prompt_templates.title: Start a tracking pre-flight
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pre-launch conversion tracking checklist for my Google Ads campaign. The primary conversion is purchase.

prompt_templates.title: Build a UTM convention
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a UTM naming convention and event specification for Google Search, Meta paid social, and LinkedIn. We track purchases and leads.

prompt_templates.title: Review supplied GA4 exports
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports for UTM gaps and event-firing issues. Mark every check pass, fail, or needs-input.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve measurement prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: Google and Meta report more conversions than GA4. Use my exports to identify tracking prerequisites, state dedup and attribution-window gaps, and produce a launch-readiness report.

output_examples.input: Check conversion tracking for Google and Meta before launch.
output: Pre-flight status: fix first because the manual test conversion is missing.
UTM rule: use lowercase source and medium values with one approved vocabulary.
Deduplication gate: declare GA4 or ecommerce order IDs as the source of truth.

output_examples.input: Build a UTM and event specification for purchase and lead campaigns.
output: UTM convention with approved values for source, medium, campaign, content, and term.
Event specification for purchase and lead events with value, currency, and deduplication IDs.
A list of modeled-data and offline-import flags to monitor after launch.

best_practices: Provide recent GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports, plus the campaign platforms and conversion actions.
Run one real manual test conversion before marking the account launch-ready.
Use a single documented source of truth and keep attribution windows, currency, and timezone comparable.
anti_patterns: Do not mark a missing export or test conversion as a pass.
Do not place emails, names, or order data in UTM parameters.
Do not treat platform-reported conversions as reconciled order counts.

faq.question: Does this skill require API access?
faq.answer: No. It works from user-provided exports and a manual test conversion. APIs are optional conveniences.

faq.question: Which platforms can it review?
faq.answer: It supports any paid platform when you provide the relevant exports and conversion details, including Google and Meta.

faq.question: What is the main output?
faq.answer: It produces a tracking pre-flight checklist, a UTM convention, an event specification, and a launch-readiness statement.

faq.question: Does it fix pixels or tags directly?
faq.answer: No. It identifies what to fix from the available evidence. It does not directly control pixel, tag-manager, or ad-platform APIs.

faq.question: Does it reconcile double-counted conversions?
faq.answer: No. It verifies that a deduplication rule exists and flags gaps. Detailed order matching belongs to a reconciliation workflow.

faq.question: Will it save my results?
faq.answer: It asks for permission before saving a pre-flight report or reusable specification for future sessions.
